notes.title: Small Update - Hiragana at level 4 will be hidden on Words/Kana submenu
notes.content:
Small change!  

Any hiragana at level 4 will now be hidden on the Words/Kana submenu. 

This makes a lot of sense because at level 4 you've mastered a hiragana and it's really just cluttering that menu up.  People who already know hiragana and set all hiragana to level 4 at the beginning of the game should also appreciate this. Now it's much easier to focus on the words and kanji you care about.

This change was suggested on the Discord server (Link: https://discord.gg/5UhSmKTu).  Certainly feel free to drop by to chat and provide your own suggestions for improving the game.

Happy learning!

Lun

notes.title: Goodbye Early Access, Hello Full Release!
notes.content:
Today we have officially left Early Access! 

Thanks to all the Early Access players who provided feedback to help improve the game. A few notable improvements include:
1. Improved Steam Deck support 
2. Multiple-choice answer option for battles
3. Warm-up Mode for battles (practice without time pressure)
4. Auto accepting correct answers (to reduce keystrokes)
5. Volume controls
6. Ability to skip all battles (even boss battles)
7. The Quiz Queen (to really hammer home those learnings)

One feature that more advanced beginners have asked about is a mode that uses kanji in dialogue in the appropriate situations.  I don't have a concrete timeline yet, but I am planning to add this in a future update.

If you haven't already, you can:

Follow us on Twitter: https://twitter.com/StudyBunnyGames

Join our Discord: https://discord.gg/VkgM3zUgmw


You can also reach out on the Steam Discussion boards if you have comments, questions, or other feedback.

Happy learning!

Lun

notes.title: Warm Up Mode is Here!
notes.content:
"Warm Up Mode" is now available in the latest update (Version 2023-6-4).

How do I use it?
Press the Ctrl key during the first few seconds of any battle to activate Warm Up Mode

What does it do?
While in Warm Up Mode...
1. Enemy attacks always miss
2. Your attacks do 0 damage 
3. Your hiragana and words will not level up

Why is this helpful?
It lets you extend battle drills for as long as you like. Thus, it's a convenient way to get lots of extra practice or to warm up if it's been awhile since you last played. 

How do I exit Warm Up Mode?
Just press the Ctrl key again

Thanks again to everyone who has left a positive review and has followed us on Steam and/or Twitter! It really helps us!

Happy Learning!

Lun

notes.title: Official release and price update
notes.content:
Hello!

We're pleased to announce that we are preparing to officially release Learn Japanese RPG: Hiragana Forbidden Speech on Steam in March. No exact date yet, but that will be determined very soon. Thank you to everyone who provided feedback through the beta testing and Early Access phases of this project.
 
In preparation for the official release, we will be updating the price.  We've kept the price down during Early Access because it didn't feel right to charge early adopters full price for a game that wasn't feature complete and still had many potential bugs lurking about. With the game now in a more polished state, we still didn't want to blindside early wishlisters on the official release date with a price update, so we're letting everyone know ahead of time that we're planning to price the game at $19.99. We arrived at this number through our own market research and based on the feedback of testers.  The new price will take effect no sooner than March 9th, so if you want to buy before then you can still get the current Early Access price.
 
It's important to us that you get great value out of the game if you decide to purchase.  That's why we provide a free demo with around three hours of gameplay and the ability to start from your last save point when you purchase the full product.  With Steam's refund policy, that allows you to play the game for about five hours before deciding whether the game is for you. 
 
This game is an introductory Japanese course designed to immerse you and get you comfortable hearing, reading, and understanding basic Japanese sentences. We've invested a lot in professional voice acting and worked very hard to make the story, conversations, and tutorials both entertaining and highly educational.
 
We've also included a lot of features to help you tweak your learning experience to your liking. For example, you can change the battle encounter rate at any time, adjust the rate that new hiragana and words are learned, put the game into reading mode (voice overs only play if you press a button), skip tutorials at your convenience, change the font, and more. Battle drills have also been optimized for speed. No long, slow animations bog things down. We also introduced the "auto-accept" feature to reduce keystrokes and save you even more time.
 
Many of these features are designed to eliminate any grind and make playing the game as convenient as possible.  We especially wanted to make second playthroughs a breeze. Because the game adapts how much Japanese you see based on your learning level, a lot of Japanese is hidden from beginners during the beginning and middle parts of the game. (If you're curious how much, start a new game in Max Japanese Mode). That content is just waiting to be found, but we knew no one would do a second playthrough if it was a grind. Once you learn everything the game teaches, you can essentially configure it to play as an interactive novel that only contains Japanese that you've been taught, sort of like the ultimate starter anime or manga.

We believe the game offers a great value and we hope you'll agree! This has been a long journey from inception to official release and we couldn't be more excited.

Thanks for your support and happy learning!
 
Lun

notes.title: Small update- More encounter rate options
notes.content:
First, there are now more Encounter Rate options to provide finer tuning for how often you have battles. You can toggle through the different rates using the 'Q' and 'Z' keys.

Second, the 'Q' key will raise the encounter rate.  The 'Z' key nows reduces the encounter rate.  

Previously, they both increased the rate and it looped back to no encounters once you reached the max encounter rate.  Not exactly great.  So hopefully this is a little more convenient and intuitive.

Happy learning!

Lun

notes.title: Small Update - Added support for additional fonts
notes.content:
The game now supports three additional TrueType fonts:

 Sarasa Fixed J
 UD Digi Kyokasho N-B
 BIZ UDGothic


If these fonts are installed on your system they should be selectable from the Font submenu. 

However, the game engine depends on system specific search paths (meaning the fonts must be installed to be available to the game). So results may vary on different systems.  

If you're having trouble with fonts, let me know on the Steam discussion board. I'm trying to put together a troubleshooting guide that will help people quickly resolve any such problems.

Happy learning!

Lun

notes.title: Update - Fix to eliminate clipped text for any font
notes.content:
The game "supports" a number of fonts, but some of them don't work as well as others.

That is to say that when you use some fonts, you'll sometimes see text getting clipped off at the end of a message box as seen here:
https://imgur.com/a/xetN7L4

The hope is that the latest update resolves this issue for all supported fonts.

I'm a little nervous about this update as this change has far reaching impacts, so please reach out to me here, Twitter, or by email at contact@studybunnygames.com if you experience any issues.

Happy learning!

Lun

notes.title: Small Update - More control of your learning
notes.content:
The latest update contains an additional menu control called "Level 1 Capacity".
https://imgur.com/a/P1rSBkX

If you've ever leveled up a bunch of level 1 hiragana/words all at once, you may have felt a bit overwhelmed at the end of the battle when you learned an equal number of new hiragana/words.

By default "Level 1 Capacity" is set to 7.  You can now take it down to 5 which may be more manageable for some people.  In other words, rather than learning 7 new words/hiragana in parallel, you should never be faced with more than 5. 

Happy learning!

Lun

notes.title: Small Update - Skipping Boss Battles
notes.content:
You can skip non-random/boss battles any time now by flipping the enemy Encounter Rate to the lowest setting using the Q or Z keys.  Formerly, this setting just impacted the frequency of random battles.

Happy learning!
